findings.what: The passage added this round is itself a fourth claim about who said what in review, and the record contradicts it. It reads: "round 8 read the artifacts and concluded a true sentence was false, because the supporting words lived in a report message rather than in the verdict JSON." The sentence round 8 blocked on was "The round-5 and round-6 reviewers each re-examined the split and rejected it, the last measuring that none of its own findings touched a scanner." Round 8's verdict (.harness/review/9483daeb7bf3....reviewer.json) refutes it on three grounds, and (c) is measurable inside the verdict JSONs alone: round 5's test-reviewer carries a finding on scripts/test_integrity.py:101 and round 6's reviewer one on scripts/java_tests.py:391, so the trailing clause is false whatever any report message said. Reproduced this round: both findings are in those files. So on the whole-sentence reading, the refuted sentence was NOT true, and the reason given for round 8's conclusion is not the reason round 8 gave. On the narrow reading -- that only "round 6 considered the split" was true, its support living in a report message -- the claim is supported by nothing in the tree AND nothing in .harness (`grep -il 'spl[ai]t' .harness/review/97bfe82bb43e*.json` returns nothing, exit 1, exactly as round 8 measured), which makes it the least checkable statement in the cell, asserted in the very clause explaining that such statements cannot be checked. The stated remedy for this defect class is to stop attributing to reviewers and rounds; the passage attributes twice more ("caught by rounds 6, 7 and 8", "round 8 read the artifacts and concluded"). The clause after the colon is deletable without losing anything the cell needs -- the point it exists to make is already carried by the words before the colon.
findings.failure_scenario: The cell is the durable, in-tree record; .harness/review/ is gitignored and dies with this machine. A milestone review, or the next author facing a rounds: argument, reads that a reviewer who DID open the artifacts still "concluded a true sentence was false", and takes it as recorded evidence that prose review of this kind over-refuses. They then discount the round-8 major -- whose actual, reproducible content is that a claim crediting two independent rounds was really one round's two roles -- and re-ship precisely the over-crediting the last three rounds removed. Concretely: the next author writes "later rounds re-validated the no-split call" again, cites M0.53's own cell as precedent that the reviewer objecting to it was wrong before, and nothing downstream can check either claim. It also leaves the tree's only record asserting a recorded major was mistaken, with the one artifact anyone can read saying otherwise.

findings.what: The cell opens "SEVEN ROUNDS, and every one of the first six found a real major" and now, in the passage added this round, names rounds 6, 7 AND 8 -- so the cell contradicts its own headline count without leaving the cell, which is checkable in the tree with no access to .harness/. The record agrees with the new text and not the headline: eight distinct staged hashes carry an M0.53 verdict, `python3 scripts/review_rounds.py 9483daeb7bf3...` prints 8, and this verdict makes nine. Rounds 7 and 8 each recorded a major too, so "every one of the first six" also reads as though round 7 found nothing. baselines/review.txt:12 opens "Seven rounds against the cap of two" and is two short by the same arithmetic. Minor rather than major because check-reviewed keys the exception on the presence of a `rounds:M0.53` line, not on the number in it (review_rounds.py counts hashes itself), and because round 6 rated the identical undercount ("rounds 2-5") a minor. Fixing it is optional under rule 11; if it is fixed, the count is in two places and both must move.
findings.failure_scenario: A milestone review reads the cap argument as excusing seven rounds when the gate would have counted nine, and the argued-list signal review.md relies on -- 'a growing argued list means somebody is being systematically overruled' -- is read two rounds light on the task with the highest round count in the milestone. Once .harness/ is gone the discrepancy is unresolvable: the reader sees a cell that says seven and then discusses a round 8, and has no artifact left to decide which number was real.
